request.prompt:
You are extracting the numeric claims of one section of a model-validation report, so that each
can be checked against the artifact it cites. Section: findings.

The prose is printed below one line per line, each prefixed with its own number and a vertical
bar. List EVERY number that appears in the prose, in the order it appears, including numbers that
appear inside a citation's logical name and numbers written with a thousands separator or a per
cent sign. For each one:

- "line" is the number printed to the left of the line the number appears on. Give the number
  only; do not copy the line's text back, and do not count the prefix itself as a number.
- "value" is the number as written, with thousands separators and the per cent sign removed:
  "3,500" is 3500, "22.0%" is 22.0.
- "unit" is "percent" when the number is written with a per cent sign, "count" for a number of
  rows, features or events, "currency", "bp" for basis points, "months" for a horizon, and
  "ratio" for every other dimensionless quantity (AUC, PSI, VIF, a coefficient, a lift).
- "metric" is what the number measures, taken from the logical name of the artifact it cites
  (auc, brier, psi, vif, calibration_slope, delta_auc, coefficient, event_rate, ...), or null.
- "split" is train, test, out_of_time or vintage_holdout, or null.
- "comparison" is "eq" for a number that equals its artifact; "delta" for a difference written
  "from a to b" or "a gap of x", whose value is the second cited artifact minus the first; and
  "ratio" for a number written as one artifact divided by another. A delta or ratio carries TWO
  adjacent citations, in that order.
- "citation" is the [[art:...]] token the number carries, copied exactly, or null when the
  sentence carries none. Do not invent a citation and do not move one from another number.
- "rounding" is the number of decimals the prose wrote when it wrote fewer than the artifact has
  (2 for a lift written 2.24), or null.

Return every number even when it has no citation: a number you leave out is still counted, and
counted against the report.

Prose:
 1| Findings are listed in the accompanying JSON. In summary:
 2| 
 3| | # | Class | Severity | Title |
 4| |---|---|---|---|
 5| | 1 | L1 | high | Perfect discrimination on all four splits indicates target leakage |
 6| | 2 | T1 | medium | Declared leakage-free feature timing is contradicted by the outcome metrics |
 7| | 3 | L2 | high | Split loan counts exceed the loan universe, implying loans shared across splits |
 8| | 4 | C1 | high | Calibration slope ≈ 2.8–2.9 on every split, with consistent positive CPR bias |
 9| | 5 | S1 | medium | Event rate varies 3.5× across splits; no PSI computed |
10| | 6 | X1 | medium | Baseline hazard has no seasoning ramp and is extrapolated far beyond support |
11| | 7 | M1 | low | Collinear rate-family and balance features; no VIF or condition number produced |
12| | 8 | D1 | info | Cross-split missingness comparison not possible from the artifacts supplied |
13| 
14| Recommendations, in priority order:
15| 
16| 1. **Do not deploy, and do not use the current results to support any MSR mark.** Treat Findings 1 and 3 as blocking.
17| 2. **Isolate the leak.** Compute single-feature AUC for all twelve features; any feature exceeding 0.90 alone is the leak. Begin with `bom_balance_log`, whose zero floor is the leading candidate, and audit the construction query for whether balance is snapshot at the start of the month or written after the payoff posts. Re-examine `burnout` on the same question, since a path functional can absorb terminal-month information.
18| 3. **Rebuild the splits with a documented, verified loan-level partition.** Intersect the identifier sets of all four splits and publish the intersections. The out-of-time split must be strictly later in calendar time and the vintage holdout must consist of origination cohorts wholly absent from training.
19| 4. **Refit and re-evaluate from scratch after (2) and (3).** Every metric in this report must be regenerated; none of them carry forward.
20| 5. **Respecify the age effect.** Add knots in the 2–30 month range so the seasoning ramp can be expressed, and either cap the projection at the estimation support or document and reserve for the extrapolation beyond age 59.
21| 6. **Address calibration explicitly** once leakage is removed, reporting the slope with a confidence interval against a pre-declared band, and produce a decile-level reliability table rather than the slope alone.
22| 7. **Produce collinearity diagnostics** (VIF and condition number over the twelve-feature design) and a rate-shock S-curve showing predicted CPR against incentive from −200bp to +200bp.
23| 8. **Commission a challenger.** No effective challenge was performed. A simple seasoning-plus-incentive logistic baseline would be sufficient to bound the value added by the current specification.


Answer with one JSON object and nothing else: no prose before or after it, no explanation, no markdown fence. It must validate against this JSON schema:
{"$defs": {"Comparison": {"description": "What the claimed value is asserted to equal.\n\n``delta`` and ``ratio`` are cited by two adjacent ``[[art:...]]`` tokens, in order (D-012).\nThe enum is not nullable: ``eq`` is the explicit default, so \"this number equals its artifact\"\nhas one spelling and not two (D-018).\n\nAttributes:\n    eq: The value matches the cited artifact.\n    delta: The value matches ``second - first``.\n    ratio: The value matches ``second / first``.", "enum": ["eq", "delta", "ratio"], "title": "Comparison", "type": "string"}, "ExtractedClaim": {"additionalProperties": false, "description": "One claim as the model returns it: the grammar minus the fields the caller already knows.\n\n``text``, ``section``, ``id`` and ``source`` are not asked for. hazard subjects.\n    vintage_holdout: One origination year held out; hazard subjects.", "enum": ["train", "test", "out_of_time", "vintage_holdout"], "title": "SplitName", "type": "string"}, "Unit": {"description": "How a number is written, which decides how it is normalised before matching.\n\nAttributes:\n    ratio: Every dimensionless quantity not written with a ``%`` -- AUC, PSI, VIF, a\n        coefficient, a lift.\n    percent: Written with a ``%``; normalised against a unit-interval artifact by dividing\n        by 100.\n    count: A number of rows, features or events. Matched to half a unit, so integers match\n        exactly.\n    currency: A money amount.\n    bp: Basis points, as a rate shock is written.\n    months: A horizon.", "enum": ["ratio", "percent", "count", "currency", "bp", "months"], "title": "Unit", "type": "string"}}, "additionalProperties": false, "description": "The JSON object the extractor is asked for: a list of claims under one key.\n\nA bare JSON array is a shape more models get wrong than a single-key object, and\n:func:`~quaestor.llm.structured.structured` validates a ``BaseModel``, not a list.\n\nAttributes:\n    claims: The claims, in the order the numbers appear.", "properties": {"claims": {"items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/ExtractedClaim"}, "title": "Claims", "type": "array"}}, "title": "ExtractedClaims", "type": "object"}
